title: Schistosomiasis: periportal fibrosis -> portal hypertension + esophageal varices
vignette: A 54-year-old man comes to the emergency department after vomiting blood. He has also had melena, fatigue, and lethargy over the last 24 hours. The patient emigrated from sub-Saharan Africa 20 years ago and occasionally returns to visit friends and family. Temperature is 37.5 C (99.5 F), blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg, and pulse is 115/min. Abdominal palpation reveals an enlarged liver and a spleen tip below the level of the umbilicus. Complete blood count shows hemoglobin 5.2 g/dL, platelets 75,000/mm3, leukocytes 8,000/mm3 with neutrophils 79%, eosinophils 15%, and lymphocytes 6%. Upper endoscopy reveals bleeding esophageal varices. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

clues.text: emigrated from sub-Saharan Africa 20 years ago and occasionally returns to visit
clues.note: Residence/travel in sub-Saharan Africa (freshwater exposure) is the key risk factor for schistosomiasis.

clues.text: enlarged liver and a spleen tip below the level of the umbilicus
clues.note: Hepatosplenomegaly with esophageal varices indicates portal hypertension from hepatic (periportal) fibrosis.
EOSINOPHILIA is an important clue to a parasitic (helminth) infection such as schistosomiasis.
Esophageal varices are a consequence of portal hypertension - here from schistosomal periportal fibrosis.

whatMatters: Portal hypertension (hepatosplenomegaly, esophageal varices, thrombocytopenia) + EOSINOPHILIA + sub-Saharan African exposure = hepatosplenic SCHISTOSOMIASIS (Schistosoma mansoni). Schistosome eggs lodge in periportal spaces, triggering fibrosis that blocks portal flow. Answer D.
strategy: Combine the geographic/freshwater exposure + portal hypertension + EOSINOPHILIA to reach schistosomiasis (the parasitic cause of noncirrhotic portal hypertension). Reject cysticercosis (Taenia solium - CNS calcified cysts, spares liver), hookworm (iron-deficiency anemia/eosinophilia but no portal hypertension), malaria (acute febrile illness, no varices/eosinophilia), and toxoplasmosis (encephalitis in AIDS).

eliminations.label: Cysticercosis - CNS, spares liver/portal system
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: infection with Taenia solium larvae, causing calcified CNS cysts and seizures. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not invade the hepatic/portal venous system or cause portal hypertension/varices. ✅ Correct if: seizures with calcified brain cysts.

eliminations.label: Hookworm - iron-deficiency anemia, no portal hypertension
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: intestinal hookworm causing chronic iron-deficiency anemia and eosinophilia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't invade the portal venous system, so hepatosplenomegaly and varices would be atypical. ✅ Correct if: iron-deficiency anemia + eosinophilia without portal hypertension.

eliminations.label: Malaria - acute febrile illness, no varices/eosinophilia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: Plasmodium infection (returning travelers) with fever, hemolysis, and possible splenomegaly. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: patients are acutely ILL/febrile, without portal hypertension, varices, or eosinophilia. ✅ Correct if: cyclic fevers with intraerythrocytic parasites.

eliminations.label: Toxoplasmosis - AIDS encephalitis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: Toxoplasma reactivation causing ring-enhancing brain lesions in advanced HIV. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes meningoencephalitis, not upper-GI bleeding from varices. ✅ Correct if: HIV with ring-enhancing CNS lesions.

reasoning: Sub-Saharan African freshwater exposure + hepatosplenomegaly + esophageal varices + eosinophilia
Eggs deposit in periportal spaces, activating stellate cells -> periportal fibrosis -> portal hypertension
mechanism: Schistosomiasis is a parasitic blood-fluke infection acquired by swimming in FRESHWATER contaminated by infected snails (intermediate host); cercariae penetrate skin, mature to adult worms, and migrate to the PORTAL/mesenteric venules (Schistosoma mansoni/japonicum) or the bladder venous plexus (S. haematobium). Adult worms release eggs into host tissue; in the liver, chronic exposure to S. mansoni eggs activates HEPATIC STELLATE CELLS and provokes a granulomatous response, depositing collagen in the PERIPORTAL spaces ('pipestem' fibrosis) that obstructs portal venous outflow. This produces NONCIRRHOTIC PORTAL HYPERTENSION: congestive splenomegaly (with hypersplenism -> thrombocytopenia), and gastroesophageal VARICES that can bleed catastrophically (as here - hematemesis, melena, anemia). EOSINOPHILIA reflects the host response to the helminth and is a key diagnostic clue. Schistosomiasis is common in rural sub-Saharan Africa. (S. haematobium instead causes urinary disease and bladder squamous cell carcinoma.) The distractors cause CNS disease (cysticercosis, toxoplasmosis), iron-deficiency anemia (hookworm), or an acute febrile hemolytic illness (malaria) - not portal-hypertensive variceal bleeding with eosinophilia.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > schistosomiasis: freshwater snails; S. mansoni/japonicum -> periportal fibrosis -> portal hypertension, hepatosplenomegaly, varices; eosinophilia; S. haematobium -> bladder cancer.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Portal hypertension + eosinophilia + African freshwater exposure = hepatosplenic schistosomiasis.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on schistosomiasis, periportal ('pipestem') fibrosis, portal hypertension, varices, or eosinophilia? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Cysticercosis/toxoplasmosis = CNS; hookworm = iron-deficiency anemia; malaria = acute febrile - none cause variceal portal hypertension with eosinophilia.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: schistosomiasis (S. mansoni) -> periportal fibrosis -> portal hypertension/varices + eosinophilia; S. haematobium -> bladder cancer.

memoryHook: Freshwater flukes lay eggs that scar the portal tracts like pipestems - backing up blood into esophageal varices - and the eosinophils give the parasite away.
